findings.title: `RunObserver` keeps one set of per-run state for all projects, and each project's `observe()` wipes the others'
findings.description:
`RunnerTenant` builds exactly one `RunObserver` for the whole tenant (`src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py`, `self._observer = RunObserver(...)` in `__init__`) and hands it to every project's `ProjectTick`. `ProjectTick.run` calls `self._observer.observe(self._run_entries(), ...)`, and `_run_entries()` returns only `self._project_id`'s unresolved `sq_run` entries. Inside `observe`:

```python
live = {entry.id for entry in entries}
self._last_poll = {k: v for k, v in self._last_poll.items() if k in live}
self._overdue &= live
self._faulted = {k: v for k, v in self._faulted.items() if k in live}
```

`live` is this project's entry ids, so observing project B deletes project A's last-poll times, overdue markers and standing faults, and vice versa. Consequences, all of them in the direction of the documented contract (`docs/process-contract.md`, "The Runner tenant", and `ProcessSettings.run_poll_interval_seconds`: *"the least time between two polls of the same launched run"*, D10):

1. **The poll interval is never honoured with more than one project.** A's `_last_poll` is gone after B is observed, so `_poll_due` returns `True` on A's next tick and every in-flight run in every project is polled on every tick. The slice design measures one `sq runs wait` at about 1 s wall / 0.7 s CPU (`project-documents/user/slices/122-slice.runner-tenant-and-control-surface.md`, "Why a poll interval"); that is exactly the cost this bound exists to prevent, and it also eats the tick deadline that `TickBudget` is meant to protect.
2. **A standing fault flaps.** `_faulted` is the mechanism that replays a poll fault on the ticks *between* polls "so a fault that stands does not look recovered (and its escalation close)". With the replay entry deleted by another project's `observe`, `_confirmed` returns `RunState.RUNNING` instead of `RunState.FAULT`; `raise_expected_faults` no longer raises `run_observation_failed` that tick, so `_close_recovered` closes the escalation, and the next poll reopens it — a new `messages` row and a new feed change each cycle, and an operator shown a fault as recovered while it persists. `_overdue` has the same shape: the marker set in `_after_launch_poll` is dropped, so the `launch_overdue` fault is skipped on the interval ticks and its escalation is closed mid-overdue.

If the prune is there to bound memory as entries disappear, it needs to be keyed to entries that are genuinely gone (per-project state, or a prune that does not use this call's entry ids). No test covers this: every observe/tick rig (`tests/runner/tick_support.py`, `tests/runner/observe_support.py`) drives a single project, and `tests/runner/test_tenant.py`'s multi-project rig never asserts on poll counts or escalation churn. A multi-project observation test — two projects, one in-flight run each, two ticks, asserting one poll per run per interval — would have caught it.

findings.title: `_in_flight_run_ids` indexes `parameters["run_id"]` directly, inside the handler that must not raise
findings.description:
```python
return [
    str(entry.parameters[PARAM_RUN_ID])
    for entry in store.unresolved_journal_entries(project_id)
    if entry.node_id == node_id and entry.kind is CommandKind.SQ_RUN
]
```

`escalate` is called from the one broad `except` in `RunnerTenant._tick_project`, after the original fault has already been logged. A `KeyError` raised here is not caught anywhere: it escapes `_tick_project`, ends the tenant's tick, and takes the process down instead of escalating, which is the opposite of the "expected faults are answers, not exceptions" doctrine stated in `faults.py`'s own module docstring. The sibling readers are careful about exactly this value — `observe._observe_one` and `finish._run_id` both treat an unusable run id as an explicit `ValueError` with a message naming the entry — so the bare subscript is inconsistent within the same stage. It is reachable when an unresolved `sq_run` entry carries no `run_id` key (pre-slice-120 rows are the documented case); recovery normally resolves or escalates those before tenants tick, so this is narrow, but the failure mode is a crash rather than an answer. Using `.get` plus the same "unusable run id" message would make the handler total.

findings.title: The "exactly one broad except" guard is a text scan, not an AST walk
findings.description:
```python
count = sum(
    path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").count("except Exception")
    for path in package.glob("*.py")
)
assert count == 1
```

The count matches a literal substring, so `except (Exception,) as error:`, `except Exception:  # ...`, an added `except BaseException`, or a `try/except` split across lines read differently from what the guard intends — and a comment or docstring containing the text inflates the count. This project's own mechanical guards walk the parsed AST and say why (`tests/test_writer_guard.py`, `tests/test_store_safety.py`: *"a call split across lines defeats a per-line search"*), and `tests/test_import_boundaries.py` — extended by this same change with rules 10 and 11 — does the same. The guard is worth keeping; matching on `ast.Try.handlers` would make it mean what it says. It is also the only mechanical check that the fault isolation boundary is singular, so its strength matters.

findings.title: `ProjectTick.wrote`'s trailing string is an expression statement, not a docstring
findings.description:
```python
self.wrote = False
"""Whether this tick wrote to the store or issued a command."""
```

A string literal after an assignment is not a docstring, so this reads as documentation while being a no-op statement (and is a candidate for ruff's `B018`, since `pyproject.toml` selects `B`; I could not run the linter to confirm which way ruff decides here). The rest of this change documents attributes with `#:` comments above the declaration — `faults.Fault`, `observed.ObservedRun`, `ProcessSettings` — so either form would be consistent; this one is neither. `CLOSED_BY: str = "runner"` in the same file is likewise the only module constant in `amoeba.runner` declared without `Final`, against `RUNNER_TENANT_NAME: Final`, `SQ_RUN_COMMAND: Final` and the rest.
